cohort: Individuals who provided data for the National Family Health Survey (NFHS 3, NFHS 4, and NFHS 5) in the northeastern States of India.
finding: The study found a substantial increase in Caesarean Section (CS) delivery rates in the northeastern States of India from 2011 to 2019, with maternal age, maternal education, obesity, and household wealth status identified as significant predictors.
mod_finding: Caesarean Section rates in the northeastern States escalated by nearly 15% over two decades (2001-2019), reaching 19.9% by 2019, with an upward trend in CS risk from 2011-2019, predicted by maternal age, education, obesity, and wealth status.
cross-section timing: Data from three rounds of the National Family Health Survey (NFHS 3, NFHS 4, and NFHS 5) collected between 2001 and 2019, with analysis focused on the period from 2011 to 2019.
